newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: FOCUS-Analysts see bulls running in Seoul market.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Analysts see bulls running in Seoul market.

text.p: Seoul stocks hit another 1997 high on Friday, the third straight record-setting session, and brokers and analysts declared the bulls had shaken off months of bad news and begun to run.
Strong investor optimism about an economic recovery and falling interest rates underpinned the market, they said.

The composite stock index rose to a new intraday yearly high of 752.29 points in early afternoon before profit-taking pulled it down. But the index closed up 3.86 points to 746.36, a new high for the year.
Yields on three-year benchmark corporate bonds declined again to 11.85 on Friday, down from 11.86 on Thursday.

"When the economy hits rock bottom and is just about to turn around, a bull is usually seen in the stock market. This is that very time," said Ahn Hyo-moon, a fund manager at Korea Investment Trust Co.
Better-than-expected macro-economic indicators fuelled investors' hopes for an economic turnaround.

Industrial output in April rose 10.7 percent year-on-year, up from an 8.4 percent rise a year earlier. Inflation, gauged by the consumer price index, rose 3.8 percent in May on the year, the lowest monthly increase in 10 years.

"April industrial output figures raise hopes of an imminent economic recovery. Despite the high growth in inventories, the prospects of recovery are bright because of improving global demand," said Han Sang-choon, economist at Daewoo Research Institute.

Chung Dong-bae, market strategist at Daewoo Securities, said the Seoul stock market hit bottom when foreign funds began flowing into the country in line with the expansion of the foreign stock ownership ceiling to 23 percent on May 2.
About 1.1 trillion won ($1.23 billion) had flowed in so far since then.
"The strengthening yen also provided further momentum," he said. "Foreign investors believed Korea would benefit most in Asia from the yen's rise."
Foreign buying interest remained strong among cheap blue chips and financial shares, which are interest-rate sensitive.
LG Electronics closed at 15,100 won after recording another yearly high of 15,400 in early trading. Daewoo Securities had the second largest volume of 1.18 million shares and ended up 300 to 11,500.
Analysts agreed the cash-flow status in the money market had been distorted as financial institutions remained fluid by cutting fresh lendings to companies.
"The abundant liquidity isn't flowing into the economy and instead is remaining in the financial industry including the stock market," Ahn said.
He said a one percentage point fall in interest rates would lead to 20 percent rise in corporate recurring profits as financial costs by domestic companies remained very high.
Brokers said that idea had begun to be reflected in stocks.
"I'm sure the market is riding a bull-run," Chung said. "The index will rise to the 800 level in June. After a consolidation, it will head for the 900 mark this year."

Brokers said the market widely ignored President Kim Young-sam's apology on Friday over election spending abuses. Kim offered no specifics and fell far short of the act of personal contrition demanded by the opposition.
"The market overcame worries about possible political turmoil on optimistic market prospects," said Kim Myung-ho of Hyundai Securities.
(Conversion $1 = 891 won)
